title: Qualitative Analysis
seo_title: Secondary 3 Chemistry: Qualitative Analysis Worksheets (O-Level 6092 with Answers)
standard_text: Describe and use tests to identify the aqueous cations aluminium, ammonium, calcium, copper(II), iron(II), iron(III) and zinc using aqueous sodium hydroxide and aqueous ammonia; the anions carbonate (by reaction with dilute acid and then limewater), chloride and iodide (with acidified silver nitrate), nitrate (by reduction with aluminium in alkaline solution) and sulfate (with acidified barium nitrate); and the gases ammonia, carbon dioxide, chlorine, hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur dioxide; deduce the identity of unknown substances from observations (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Chemistry 6092 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Chemistry worksheets on qualitative analysis: tests for cations with sodium hydroxide and ammonia, tests for anions and gases, and identifying unknown salts. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Use NaOH and NH₃ to identify cations.
key_sub: Al³⁺ and Zn²⁺: tell them apart with excess NH₃.
body_html:
How to think about it

Each ion gives a characteristic result with a reagent.

  • NaOH: Al³⁺, Zn²⁺ white, soluble in excess; Ca²⁺ white, insoluble; Cu²⁺ light blue; Fe²⁺ green; Fe³⁺ red-brown; NH₄⁺ gives ammonia on warming.
  • NH₃(aq): Zn²⁺ white, dissolves in excess; Al³⁺ white, does not; Cu²⁺ light blue, dissolves to a dark blue solution; Ca²⁺ no precipitate.
  • Anions: CO₃²⁻ fizzes with acid (CO₂); Cl⁻ white and I⁻ yellow with acidified AgNO₃; SO₄²⁻ white with acidified Ba(NO₃)₂; NO₃⁻ gives NH₃ with NaOH and Al.
  • Gases: H₂ pops, O₂ relights a glowing splint, CO₂ turns limewater milky, NH₃ turns red litmus blue, Cl₂ bleaches litmus, SO₂ decolourises acidified KMnO₄.
Example

White precipitate with NaOH, dissolves in excess; with excess NH₃ it stays. Cation?

Al³⁺ or Zn²⁺ from NaOH

Zn²⁺ would dissolve in NH₃

Answer: Al³⁺

Example

Acidified Ba(NO₃)₂ gives a white precipitate. Anion?

Answer: sulfate

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up Al³⁺ and Zn²⁺: only Zn(OH)₂ dissolves in excess aqueous ammonia.
  • Writing a red-brown precipitate for Fe²⁺ (it is green; Fe³⁺ is red-brown).
  • Acidifying with hydrochloric acid before the chloride test.
  • Saying carbon dioxide relights a glowing splint (that is oxygen).

faq.q: How do you tell aluminium ions from zinc ions?
faq.a: Both give white precipitates that dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide. With excess aqueous ammonia, only the zinc precipitate dissolves.

faq.q: How do you test for chloride and sulfate ions?
faq.a: Acidify with dilute nitric acid. Add aqueous silver nitrate: a white precipitate shows chloride. Add aqueous barium nitrate: a white precipitate shows sulfate.

faq.q: What are the tests for common gases?
faq.a: Hydrogen pops with a lighted splint, oxygen relights a glowing splint, carbon dioxide turns limewater milky, ammonia turns damp red litmus blue, chlorine bleaches damp litmus and sulfur dioxide decolourises acidified potassium manganate(VII).

sets.title: Tests for cations with sodium hydroxide

items.q: A green precipitate with sodium hydroxide slowly turns brown at the surface on standing. Why?
c: It reacts with light to make chlorine.
Iron(II) hydroxide is oxidised by air to iron(III) hydroxide.
items.e: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺.

items.q: What colour is an aqueous solution containing iron(III) ions (with a colourless anion)?
items.e: Transition metal ions are often coloured: Cu²⁺ blue, Fe²⁺ pale green, Fe³⁺ yellow-brown.

items.q: Aqueous sodium hydroxide is added to a solution of zinc ions, first a little and then in excess. What is seen?

white precipitate; white precipitate is insoluble in excess
white precipitate; precipitate dissolves, giving a colourless solution
items.e: zinc, Zn²⁺: with NaOH, white precipitate; in excess, precipitate dissolves, giving a colourless solution.

items.q: A solution gives a white precipitate with aqueous sodium hydroxide, which dissolves in excess. With aqueous ammonia it gives a white precipitate, which dissolves in excess. Which cation is present?
items.e: Use both reagents: zinc, Zn²⁺.

items.q: Which cation gives a dark blue solution with excess aqueous ammonia?
items.e: A light blue precipitate forms first.

items.q: A solution gives a green precipitate with aqueous sodium hydroxide, which does not dissolve in excess. With aqueous ammonia it gives a green precipitate, which does not dissolve in excess. Which cation is present?
items.e: Use both reagents: iron(II), Fe²⁺.

items.e: Transition metal ions are often coloured: Cu²⁺ blue, Fe²⁺ pale green, Fe³⁺ yellow-brown.

c: It reacts with silver nitrate to give hydrogen.
It contains chloride ions, which would give a white precipitate anyway.

items.q: Two tests are done on a substance X. Test 1: Aqueous ammonia gives a white precipitate that dissolves in excess. Test 2: Acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add aqueous barium nitrate: white precipitate. What is X?
items.e: The first test shows the zinc ion and the second shows the sulfate ion.
